sec: Childhood NS: hypoalbuminemia & edema theories · p757

items.q: Which of these belongs to the RIGHT-hand branch of the underfill flowchart rather than the left-hand one?
opts: Transfer of fluid from capillaries to interstitium
items.exp: After 'Transfer of fluid from capillaries to interstitium' the chart splits: left to periorbital puffiness and pedal edema (extravascular edema), right to ↓ effective circulatory volume → 2° RAS activation → release of aldosterone → retention of Na+ and water (intravascular edema). (Book p757)

items.q: Fill up: In the underfill chain, the step that sits between secondary RAS activation and retention of sodium and water is the release of ______.
items.exp: The printed right-hand chain is ↓ effective circulatory volume → 2° RAS activation → Release of aldosterone → Retention of Na+, water (Intravascular edema). (Book p757)

items.q: A nephrotic child has periorbital puffiness, pedal edema, pulse 130 and blood pressure 78/50. The underfill chart accounts for the low pressure by:
opts: Fluid transfer into the interstitium lowering the effective circulatory volume
Primary RAS activation from streptococcal plasmin release
ANP resistance retaining sodium in the intravascular space
items.exp: In underfill, loss of capillary oncotic pressure shifts fluid to the interstitium; the same shift that produces extravascular edema drops the effective circulating volume and triggers secondary RAS activation. (Book p757)

items.q: The hypoalbuminemia block gives two mechanisms: urinary loss of albumin and reduced compensation by the liver.
opts: True — both bullets are printed under HYPOALBUMINEMIA
False — the liver is said to over-compensate
False — only urinary loss is listed
True — and a third bullet names impaired intestinal absorption
items.exp: The two bullets read 'urinary loss of albumin' and '↓ compensation by liver'; the nail figure beneath the Sign heading shows Muehrcke's line. (Book p757)
